items.text: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) launch eight drone and land attacks across El Obeid, North Kordofan. Two people are reported to be killed during the attacks. ((Reuters))

RSF launch drone strikes across multiple cities in Sudan, including its capital Khartoum, Bahri, and Omdurman in Khartoum State and the River Nile cites of Ad-Damir, and Atbara. ((AFP via Arab News)) ((The National News))
A drone strike is reported on an Zawiya electrical substation in western Libya, causing a fire and power outages. ((The Hill))

Two soldiers were killed and at least seventeen more wounded (all members of the 9th Brigade). The attack occurred after military personnel were requeried to examine a suspicious cylinder in a road of the locality of El Quebradón, Algeciras, Huila, subsequently were ambushed for suspected members of the Iván Diaz Front. ((El Colombiano))

A failed attack against the Tayoltita Airfield, in San Dimas Municipality, Durango, leaves one gunmen killed and two soldiers wounded. Authorities deploy an operative in the zone securing the area and search for the rest of the attackers. ((La Jornada))
A woman is killed and 172 other people are rescued after a ferry catches fire off the coast of Bali, Indonesia. ((AFP via RFI))
Four people are killed, including the perpetrator, in shooting and stabbing attacks at a daycare and a house in Hopkins, Minnesota, United States. ((CBS News))

Cook Islanders vote to elect all 24 seats of Parliament amid a cost-of-living crisis and debate regarding a past partnership agreement with China. Incumbent prime minister Mark Brown faces a challenge from Cook Islands United leader Teariki Heather. ((RNZ)) ((The Guardian))
The Rapid Support Forces-appointed governor of Sudan's Kordofan region, Hamad Mohammad Hamad Khalifa, resigns and will defect. ((Sudan Tribune)) ((Al-Arabiya))

A total solar eclipse occurs in Greenland, Iceland, and Spain, with partial eclipses visible over much of northern North America, Europe (except most of Ukraine, Greece, Bulgaria and Russia), northwestern Africa and northern Asian Russia. It is the first total eclipse observable in mainland Europe since the solar eclipse of August 11, 1999. ((Time and Date)) ((EclipseWise))

Astronomers who have spent four years trying to understand the mysterious little red dots found by the James Webb Space Telescope announce in Nature that it marks the discovery of a new type of astrophysical object, the black hole star. The first object classed as such, MoM-BH*-1, in the constellation of Cetus, is the size of the Solar System and emits a pure light that outshines its host galaxy. ((The Guardian)) ((PopSci))
